transcript: If you didn't make it to Duke & Roya at the Lortel before it reached its untimely early closing this past weekend, I wouldn't sweat it. Despite a handful of great moments, it wasn't rendered sharply enough to leave any lasting impression, for me at least. I did quite enjoy all of the performances from this small cast of four, and the chemistry between the titular characters was really great. A bit of a “right person, wrong place and time” kind of love story, this play is about an American rapper played by Jay Ellis who forms an unexpected connection with an interpreter he meets in Afghanistan played by Stephanie Nur. The progression of their relationship and the snapshots we get of these characters are certainly interesting, but this comes at the cost of other plot points which felt pretty underdeveloped and random at times. After Act 1, the play's focus got fuzzy and it wasn't able to maintain momentum and tie up all the loose ends that it had introduced. As a character study, this had a lot to offer, but as a political drama, which also seemed to be a significant piece of this play, it didn't quite deliver. With that, another playbill for my collection.
